text: How can you describe the large pit inside this cut peach in a full sentence?
This peach has a pit.
How does the sentence change when you describe two peaches with one pit in each?
These peaches have pits.
Can you fix one word in the sentence about the small seeds inside this cut cucumber?
This cucumber has seeds.
How can you describe the large pit inside this cut mango in a full sentence?
This mango has a pit.
How can you describe what is inside both cut tomatoes in a full sentence?
These tomatoes have seeds.
How can you describe the large pit inside this cut avocado in a full sentence?
This avocado has a pit.
Starting with I, can you tell Leo about your two mangoes and his one mango as if you are Mia?
I have two mangoes and you have one mango.
How does the sentence change when Leo tells Mia about both amounts, starting with his own mango?
I have one mango and you have two mangoes.
You are telling Ben about his three peaches, so can you fix one word in the sentence?
You have three peaches.
Can you tell your friend about your four oranges and his two oranges, using I and you in one sentence?
I have four oranges and you have two oranges.
How can Max tell Lily about both amounts, starting with his own two oranges?
I have two oranges and you have four oranges.
Pretend you are Sam with one avocado and Eva has three, so how can you tell her about both amounts?
I have one avocado and you have three avocados.
Pretend you are Mia with three tomatoes while Leo has two, so how can you tell us only your own amount?
I have three tomatoes.
How can Mia and Leo tell us their total when they put all three and two tomatoes together?
We have five tomatoes.
Lily and Max put two peaches and four peaches together, so can you fix one word in their sentence?
We have six peaches.
You have two mangoes and Sam has three, so how can you tell us how many you have together?
We have five mangoes.
How can you say the addition for four oranges plus three oranges using plus and equals?
Four plus three equals seven.
You have one cucumber and Lily has four, so how can you tell us how many you have together?
We have five cucumbers.
Pretend you are Mia sharing oranges with Leo, so how can you ask about your total number of oranges?
How many oranges do we have?
How does your question change when you ask Ben about only his oranges?
How many oranges do you have?
Can you fix one word in this question about the number of Kim's mangoes?
How many mangoes do you have?
You and Max are putting your peaches together, so how can you ask about your total?
How many peaches do we have?
How can you ask Sam about the number of tomatoes he has?
How many tomatoes do you have?
You and Lily are putting your avocados together, so how can you ask about your total?
How many avocados do we have?
